headline: 83.8% right if a tautomer or salt may differ. Of the 933 the model marked high-confidence, 90.2% are exact. Input is RDKit's own 1500 px layout — the best of eight ways of drawing the same molecules, catalogued below.
footer: Stage 3 only: one already-cropped depiction per image, no figure extraction and no segmentation. Scored against PubChem structures fetched in the same request batch as the images.

arms.name: RDKit 1500, fresh layout
arms.note: Draw it yourself at 1500 px. The arm the page reports.

arms.name: RDKit 300
arms.note: Same layout, smaller canvas. Costs four points.

arms.name: PubChem re-rendered 1500
arms.note: PubChem's own 2D coordinates, redrawn with stroke width scaled to the canvas.

arms.name: PubChem 300 + white remap
arms.note: Near-white background forced to true white. Best result from repairing a supplied image.

arms.name: PubChem white + upscaled 1200
arms.note: Remap, then resample to 1200 px. Resampling adds nothing.

arms.name: PubChem 300, as supplied
arms.note: What you get fetching PubChem at the default size.

arms.name: PubChem 1500, as supplied
arms.note: PubChem's own large PNG. Zero correct, on all 1210, in four independent batches.

armsNote: All eight arms on the same 760 compounds — the largest set every arm covers. Strict is the string as emitted, which is what you get pasting it into a database. Graded allows a tautomer, a charge or a salt to differ. Phantom is the share of predictions carrying a stray disconnected fragment welded on beside an otherwise correct molecule.
